{{Short description|Type of statistical test}}
A '''portmanteau test''' is a type of [[statistical hypothesis test]] in which the [[null hypothesis]] is well specified, but the [[alternative hypothesis]] is more loosely specified. Tests constructed in this context can have the property of being at least moderately [[statistical power|powerful]] against a wide range of departures from the null hypothesis. Thus, in [[applied statistics]], a portmanteau test provides a reasonable way of proceeding as a general check of a [[statistical model|model's]] match to a dataset where there are many different ways in which the model may depart from the underlying [[data collection|data generating process]]. The use of such tests avoids having to be very specific about the particular type of departure being tested.

==Examples==

In [[time series analysis]], two well-known versions of a '''portmanteau test''' are available for testing for [[autocorrelation]] in the residuals of a model: it tests whether any of a group of [[autocorrelation]]s of the residual [[time series]] are different from zero.  This test is the [[Ljung–Box test]],<ref name=LB>{{cite journal |last=Ljung |first=G. M. |last2=Box |first2=G. E. P. |title=On a measure of lack of fit in time series models |journal=[[Biometrika]] |volume=65 |year=1978 |issue=2 |pages=297–303 |doi=10.1093/biomet/65.2.297 |url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA049397.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170923180644/http://www.dtic.mil/get-tr-doc/pdf?AD=ADA049397 |url-status=live |archive-date=September 23, 2017 }}</ref> which is an improved version of the [[Box–Pierce test]],<ref>{{cite journal |last=Box |first=G. E. P. |last2=Pierce |first2=D. A. |title=Distribution of Residual Autocorrelations in Autoregressive-Integrated Moving Average Time Series Models |journal=[[Journal of the American Statistical Association]] |volume=65 |year=1970 |issue=332 |pages=1509–1526 |jstor=2284333 |doi=10.1080/01621459.1970.10481180 }}</ref> having been devised at essentially the same time; a seemingly trivial simplification (omitted in the improved test) was found to have a deleterious effect.<ref name=LB/> This portmanteau test is useful in working with [[ARIMA]] models.

In the context of [[regression analysis]], including regression analysis with [[time series]] structures, a '''portmanteau test''' has been devised,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Castle |first=Jennifer L. |last2=Hendry |first2=David F. |year=2010 |title=A Low-Dimension Portmanteau Test for Non-linearity |journal=[[Journal of Econometrics]] |volume=158 |issue=2 |pages=231–245 |doi=10.1016/j.jeconom.2010.01.006|url=https://www.economics.ox.ac.uk/materials/papers/4214/paper471.pdf }}</ref> which allows a general test to be made for the possibility that a range of types nonlinear transformations of combinations of the [[independent and dependent variables|explanatory variables]] should have been included in addition to a selected model structure.<ref>{{cite book |last=Enders |first=W. |authorlink=Walter Enders|title=Applied Econometric Time Series |url=https://archive.org/details/appliedeconometr00ende_724 |url-access=limited |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |year=1995 |location=New York |isbn=0471039411 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/appliedeconometr00ende_724/page/n47 86]–87 }}</ref>
